channel.title: Via Fidelitatis
channel.description: Faithful financial independence for Catholic families

item.title: Leave the Two Denarii: Lessons from the Jericho Road
item.description: The Samaritan set the wounded man on his own animal, then left two denarii with the innkeeper and promised to cover whatever else the night cost. A household with no open tab cannot make that promise.

item.title: Hand Him the Sealed Bond: Lessons from Tobias
item.description: Tobit put the sealed bond in his son's hand: ten talents of silver left with Gabael, not to be spent on the road. Raphael walked with the boy until the purse was paid out whole.

item.title: Open the Christmas Shoes: Lessons from St. Thérèse
item.description: Thérèse heard her father say the shoes by the hearth would be filled for the last time. She dried the tears, ran downstairs, and opened them with joy. A denied want does not have to become a purchase.

item.title: Copy the Manuscript: Lessons from St. Jerome
item.description: Jerome sat in a Bethlehem cave and copied Hebrew into Latin so the Church would not starve for the Word. Households that keep surplus unclaimed can still fund that same slow work of formation.

item.title: Cast Down the Dragon: Lessons from St. Michael
item.description: Michael and his angels threw the dragon down. Households that leave a share of surplus unclaimed can still refuse the quieter snare that every extra dollar is already spoken for.

item.title: Grind the Wheat: Lessons from St. Wenceslaus
item.description: St. Wenceslaus rose at night, barefoot, to grind wheat and bake bread for the poor with his own hands. Households that leave surplus unclaimed can still answer that same quiet call.

item.title: Compose the Hymn: Lessons from Blessed Herman
item.description: Born twisted and barely able to speak, Blessed Herman still wrote the Salve Regina from his cell. Households that keep real surplus free can still offer the better part when health or schedule feels locked.

item.title: Ransom the Captive: Lessons from Our Lady of Mercy
item.description: Peter Nolasco looked at the Christian slaves and said, “Behold eternal treasures which never fail.” Households that keep real surplus free can treat the next captive need the same way.

item.title: Offer the First Coin: Lessons from Padre Pio
item.description: When the hospital was only an idea, Padre Pio pulled a single coin from his pocket and handed it over as the first gift. Families that treat every small surplus the same way keep the ledger open for real works of mercy.

item.title: Stand with the Legion: Lessons from St. Maurice
item.description: When the emperor ordered sacrifice to the gods, Maurice and the Theban Legion refused as one body. Households that keep unclaimed surplus can make the same quiet refusal when fidelity costs a job, a raise, or a lifestyle.

item.title: Leave the Tax Booth: Lessons from St. Matthew
item.description: Matthew rose from the customs post the moment Jesus said “Follow me.” Households that release the claim on every extra dollar keep the same free hand for the next call of mercy or vocation.

item.title: Travel Light: Lessons from St. Joseph of Cupertino
item.description: On his deathbed Joseph of Cupertino told his superior he had nothing left to resign. Households that keep no fixed claims on surplus can answer the next transfer without panic.

item.title: Sell the Tapestries: Lessons from St. Robert Bellarmine
item.description: When famine hit Rome, Cardinal Bellarmine tore the tapestries from his walls and sold them for the poor. “The walls won’t catch cold,” he said. Families that keep real surplus can do the same with their own comforts.

item.title: Give Away the Inheritance: Lessons from St. Cyprian
item.description: Cyprian distributed his entire fortune to the poor the hour he turned to Christ. Households that release the claim on surplus keep the same free hand for mercy when the need appears.

item.title: Stand Beside the Cross: Lessons from Our Lady of Sorrows
item.description: Mary stood at the foot of the Cross while others fled. A household that keeps real margin can stay present when sorrow lands instead of scrambling for the next dollar or distraction.

item.title: Leave Room for the Cross: Lessons from Its Exaltation
item.description: Christ emptied Himself and took the form of a slave. Households that claim every dollar have no free hand when the real cross arrives.
